name: Viet Hai Village
kicker: Valley village reached on foot through the park
summary: Remote village in a limestone valley: hike 8–12 km through the national park past Ao Ếch, or come by boat. About 80 houses of bamboo, wood, and earth sit near the Lan Ha shore. Go when you want a full day on foot; skip it on a short stay.
fee: Park ticket, 160,000 đồng for an adult
getThere: Trek through the park, or boat from Bến Bèo
heroCaption: Fields and limestone peaks around Việt Hải
body: Việt Hải is a small village in a valley on the Lan Ha side of Cát Bà, ringed by limestone hills. About 80 houses are built of bamboo, wood, leaves, and earth.

The trek starts in the national park and passes Ao Ếch, a pool in the forest. In summer it holds fresh water. In the dry season the bed turns firm and slightly springy, and you can walk across it. The whole route is 8–12 km, depending on where you start.
April to September is the easier season for the walk, and winter is possible too. You can also arrive by boat from Bến Bèo or on a Lan Ha cruise.

figures.caption: The forest track toward Việt Hải
figures.alt: A narrow road under a tunnel of trees on the way to Viet Hai

gettingThere: Walk in from the national park by way of Ao Ếch, 8–12 km, or take a boat from Bến Bèo to the Lan Ha shore below the village.

legs.heading: From the national park
legs.body: On foot past Ao Ếch, 8–12 km.

legs.heading: From Cat Ba town
legs.body: By boat from Bến Bèo, or as a stop on a Lan Ha cruise.

admissionNote: The walk crosses the national park, so the park ticket applies: from 1 January 2026, 160,000 đồng for an adult and 80,000 đồng for a child from age 6. Under 6 is free.
